claims.text: At stage-2 deploy.sh runs scripts/dev-secrets.sh (creates .env if missing), then scripts/k8s/secrets.sh, then lists the Secrets by name (kubectl get secrets -o name), before any other manifest except the namespace.

secrets.sh builds the Secrets db, api and keycloak from variables read out of .env, piping kubectl create secret generic --dry-run=client -o yaml into kubectl apply, so no Secret manifest is written to a file or kept in Git.
The api Secret's ConnectionStrings__Default contains the same $POSTGRES_PASSWORD as the db Secret's POSTGRES_PASSWORD.
kubectl create secret ... --dry-run=client -o yaml prints a Secret manifest whose data field holds each value base64-encoded; base64 -d reverses it with no key.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Secrets (Secret data is base64-encoded, not encrypted); kubectl create secret generic reference

claims.text: Argo CD compares, syncs, self-heals and prunes only resources from the Application's source or carrying its tracking label/annotation; a Secret created by kubectl outside Git is not managed, so Argo CD neither recreates it when deleted nor records its changes.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: User Guide > Resource Tracking; Automated Sync Policy (prune, self-heal)

claims.text: A file removed in a later commit stays in the earlier commits and in every existing clone; removing it from Git history requires rewriting history, so a leaked value must be changed.
claims.source_hint: Git docs: git-filter-branch (WARNING / rewriting history); GitHub docs: Removing sensitive data from a repository

claims.text: Two designs keep Secrets declared in Git: an encrypted object that an in-cluster component decrypts into a Secret (Argo CD applies it like any manifest, holds no key), or a reference from which an in-cluster component copies the value out of a secret store.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Operator Manual > Secret Management (destination-cluster secret management vs manifest generation)

claims.text: Some setups decrypt during manifest generation, through a plugin of Argo CD, which then holds the key; the generated manifests sit in plain text in Argo CD's cache, readable by anyone with access to its Redis or repo-server.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Operator Manual > Secret Management (manifest generation-based secret management, drawbacks)

claims.text: scripts/dev-secrets.sh writes the fixed POSTGRES_PASSWORD=donhang-dev-password into a new .env, and a random KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD (openssl rand -hex 16) on each machine where it is missing, so two deployers' Keycloak admin passwords differ.

deploy.sh at stage-2 also builds the ConfigMaps db-init and keycloak-realm by command (kubectl create configmap --from-file ... --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply); their content is not secret, and stage-3 commits them as envs/staging/db-init.yaml and keycloak-realm.yaml.
From stage-3 staging's folder of the config repository holds its Secrets encrypted (added by scripts/devops/seal-secrets.sh); production's folder holds none.
Encrypting into Git fits when the lab should need nothing beyond the cluster and the repository; a separate secret store fits when many systems share secrets or values change without a commit.
Anyone who can clone a private repository, including reviewers and Argo CD, can read every value in it; private limits who clones, not what a clone shows.

A container whose secretKeyRef names a missing Secret does not start; it waits with reason CreateContainerConfigError. In staging (db wave 0, api wave 2) the sync then stops at wave 0 and the api is never applied.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Secrets (non-optional Secrets); examples/don-hang outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/dr-drill-without-sealing-key.txt:20-27; envs/staging/db.yaml, api.yaml sync-wave

claims.text: At stage-2 the db and api Deployments read Secrets through secretKeyRef (deploy/k8s/db.yaml, api.yaml).
scripts/devops/argocd-install.sh at stage-3 gives Argo CD no decryption key or plugin; it applies a pinned install manifest.
In the example repository, git check-ignore -v .env prints '.gitignore:1:.env' then a tab and '.env'; git log --all --oneline -- .env prints nothing, since .env was never committed.
claims.source_hint: run 2026-10-13 in examples/don-hang; .gitignore:1 @ stage-2; Git docs: git-check-ignore (-v output format)
